Get one element of each sample

Source: R/chrom_list-methods.R
get_element.Rd

Extracts the same element from every sample of a chrom_list whose samples are themselves lists, such as the output of read_chroms with several what values (e.g. c("dad", "instrument")). The result has one chromatogram per sample, which packages that expect a list of chromatograms, such as chromatographR, accept as is.

Usage

get_element(x, what)

Arguments

x

A chrom_list whose samples are lists of elements.

what

The element to extract: a single name (e.g. "dad"), or a vector of names for a nested element (e.g. c("instrument", "PMP1, Pressure")). A nested element can also be written as one string split at the first colon, as in "instrument:PMP1, Pressure", unless that string is itself an element name.

Value

A list of the extracted chromatograms, with the names and class of x.

See also

read_chroms, extract_metadata

Examples

path <- system.file("extdata", "benzoxazinoid_standards", "BENZOS_250PPM.D",
                    package = "chromConverter")
run <- read_chroms(path, format_in = "agilent_d",
                   what = c("chroms", "instrument"), progress_bar = FALSE)
pressure <- get_element(run, "instrument:PMP1, Pressure")
head(pressure[[1]])
#>       intensity
#> 0        169.77
#> 0.005    157.60
#> 0.01     157.73
#> 0.015    158.26
#> 0.02     158.66
#> 0.025    158.99
